title: Random Forests
text: A random forest is an ensemble of many decision trees, each trained on a random subset of the training data and a random subset of features. The final prediction is made by combining the predictions of all the individual trees, typically by majority vote for classification or averaging for regression. Because each tree sees slightly different data, the errors of individual trees tend to cancel out, making random forests more robust and less prone to overfitting than a single decision tree.

title: Principal Component Analysis
text: Principal component analysis, or PCA, is an unsupervised technique for reducing the number of features in a dataset while preserving as much variance as possible. PCA works by finding new axes, called principal components, that are linear combinations of the original features and are ordered by how much variance they explain. Projecting data onto the first few principal components often preserves most of the important structure while significantly reducing dimensionality, which helps with visualization and can reduce overfitting.

title: Hyperparameter Tuning
text: Hyperparameters are configuration values for a machine learning model that are set before training begins, such as the learning rate, the number of layers, or the regularization strength, as opposed to parameters like weights that are learned during training. Hyperparameter tuning is the process of searching for the combination of hyperparameters that yields the best performance on a validation set. Common tuning strategies include grid search, which exhaustively tries every combination, and random search, which samples combinations at random and often finds good settings more efficiently.

title: Recurrent Neural Networks
text: A recurrent neural network, or RNN, is a type of neural network designed for sequential data, where the output at each step depends on both the current input and a hidden state carried over from previous steps. This hidden state acts as a form of memory, allowing the network to model dependencies across time. Traditional RNNs struggle to learn long-range dependencies due to vanishing gradients, which led to the development of variants like long short-term memory networks that are better at retaining information over longer sequences.

title: Precision and Recall
text: Precision and recall are two metrics used to evaluate classification models, especially when classes are imbalanced. Precision measures the fraction of positive predictions that are actually correct, while recall measures the fraction of actual positive examples that the model correctly identified. There is often a tradeoff between the two: increasing recall by predicting positive more often tends to lower precision, and vice versa. The F1 score combines precision and recall into a single number using their harmonic mean.
